(By Sri. B. Anjaneyalu, Advocate)
 :Judgment:

1. The petitioner filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injures sustained by him in the road traffic accident occurred on 15.08.2024.
2.

It is the case of the petitioner that, on 15.08.2024 at about 11.00 a.m., within the jurisdiction of Kaggalipura Police Station, near Somanahalli Toll, Kanakapura - Bengaluru main road, when the Petitioner was riding the unoffending Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-13-Y-4613 along with Muzamil Pasha and Sakib Khan as pillion riders, at 3 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.7169/2024 that time the accused being the rider of the offending Bullet Motor Cycle bearing reg. KA-05-QD-5332,
instead of riding the same from Kanakapura - Bengaluru main road by approaching the left side toll,
he drove the same in a opposite direction from Bengaluru - Kanakapura road toll in a high speed,
rash and negligent manner so as to endangering human life and dashed against the unoffending vehicle, as a result, Petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
Thereafter Petitioner was shifted to CDSIMER Hosptial, Harohalli and for higher treatment he was shifted to KIMS Hospital, Bengaluru wherein he was treated as inpatient.
He has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenditure and other incidental charges.
In this regard the Petitioner has lodged complaint before the Kaggalipura police station.

Accordingly, a case was registered in their Crime No.271/2024 and prepared F.I.R.
for the offence punishable under sections 281 and 125(b) of BNS and submitted to the jurisdictional judicial Magistrate and the superior officers and investigation was taken up by the investigating Officer.
3.

Further it is contended that, prior to the alleged accident the Petitioner was hale, healthy and he was 4 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.7169/2024 aged about 34 years and he was doing Nutrition sales men and earning sum of Rs.30,000/- p.m.
Due to the injuries sustained in the alleged accident he lost his income and future prospective life, happiness, and earning capacity and become disabled and dependent.
The alleged accident is occurred due to fault and negligence act of the rider of the offending Bullet Motor Cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-QD-5332.
Respondent No.1 is the RC owner and Respondent No.2 is the Insurer of the said offending vehicle,
as such the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to Petitioner.
Hence Petitioner filed the present claim petition for seeking compensation.

2 4.
In response to the notice, the Respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared before the court through their counsels and filed their respective written statements.

5. In the written statement of respondent No.1, she has admitted that she is the owner of the offending vehicle and denied the petition averments in part including age, avocation, income and negligence attributed against the driver of the offending vehicle and contended that the offending vehicle was insured with Respondent No.2/Insurance company 5 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.7169/2024 and any liability, i.e., fastened on him would have to be indemnify by the Respondent No.1 and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
6.

In the written statement of respondent No.2, Respondent No.2 the Insurance Company has admitting that, the offending Bullet Motor Cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-QD-5332 was duly insured with it and the same is valid on the date of the accident and denied the petition averments in part.
Further it has contended that the insured vehicle is not involved in the accident.
The insurer liability is subjected to validity of the DL and other documents as per the law.
Further it is alleged that there is no compliance of provision under Section 134(C), 158(6) of M.V. Act.
Further it is contended that the alleged accident is occurred due to fault of the Petitioner and no fault of the rider of the offending vehicle.
As such the insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation and in order to get compensation the Petitioner has constrained to filed the present claim petition.

Further it is denied that the age, income and occupation of the Petitioner and the petition is false and frivolous in the eye of law and the quantum of compensation claimed by the claimants is exorbitant and reserves the right u/s.170 of M.V. 6 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.7169/2024 Act., and violated terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
Hence sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
7. On the basis of above pleadings following Issues were framed.

:: I S S U E S ::
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that on 15-08-2024 at about 11-00 a.m, when he was riding a Motor Cycle bearing registration No.KA-13-Y- 4613 from Bengaluru towards Kanakapura side slowly and cautiously near Somanahalli toll,
Kanakapura - Bengaluru Road, Uttarahalli Hobli, Bengaluru south, Bengaluru city at that time, the driver of offending Bullet Motor Cycle bearing registration No.KA- 05-QD-5332 drove the same from Kanakapura side towards Bengaluru side in a rash or negligent manner and dashed against his Motor Cycle.
As a result of forced impact, the Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries?
2. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

from whom?
3. What order or award?

The Respondents have not adduced any evidence.
9. Heard the arguments from both side.

10. My findings to the above referred Issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 :- In the affirmative  Issue No.2 :- Partly in the affirmative  Issue No.3 :- As per final order,
for the following.......

:REASONS:
11.
Issue No.1:- This petition is filed u/s.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the alleged accident.

12. The petitioner in the petition has contended that, on 15.08.2024 at about 11.00 a.m., within the jurisdiction of Kaggalipura Police Station, near Somanahalli Toll, Kanakapura - Bengaluru main road, when the Petitioner was riding the unoffending Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg.

No.KA-13-Y-4613 8 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.7169/2024 along with Muzamil Pasha and Sakib Khan as pillion riders, at that time the accused being the rider of the offending Bullet Motor Cycle bearing reg. KA-05-QD- 5332, instead of riding the same from Kanakapura - Bengaluru main road by approaching the left side toll, he drove the same in a opposite direction from Bengaluru - Kanakapura road toll in a high speed, rash and negligent manner so as to endangering human life and dashed against the unoffending vehicle, as a result, Petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
Thereafter Petitioner was shifted to CDSIMER Hosptial, Harohalli and for higher treatment he was shifted to KIMS Hospital, Bengaluru wherein he was treated as inpatient.
It is contended that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.

The respondent No.1 by admitting that she is the owner of the offending vehicle and denied the petition averments and her version is that, the offending vehicle was insured with Respondent No.2/Insurance company and any liability, i.e., fastened on her would have to be indemnify by the Respondent No.2 and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.

The Respondent No.2 admitted the alleged accident and its version is that, the alleged accident occurred due to the negligence 9 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.7169/2024 and fault of the rider of the unoffending vehicle and no fault of the rider of the offending vehicle, however, slowly he may be driving and therefore he cannot be held to be negligent.
Further it is alleged that, rider of the offending vehicle is not possessing valid D.L, at the time of alleged accident.
As such the insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation and in order to obtain the compensation Petitioners have constrained to filed the present claim petition.

Further it is denied that the age, income and occupation of the Petitioner and the petition is false and frivolous in the eye of law and the quantum of compensation claimed by the claimants is exorbitant and sought for dismissal of the petition.
Nawaz Khan vs Geethamma P on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33275874/
4 13.
The burden to prove the framed issues lies on the Petitioner.

Hence, in order to prove his case,
the Petitioner himself examined as P.W.1 and he has reiterated the entire petition averments and contentions taken in the course of claim petition in his evidence before this Court and also produced as many as Exs.P.1 to P.11 documents.
Therefore, there is no necessity to repeat those facts again.
In support of the Petitioner's case and in order to substantiate the oral evidence of P.W.1, the 10 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.7169/2024 Petitioner has examined one witness by name Dr.Nagaraj.B.N., as PW.2.
I have gone through the documents produced by the PW-1.

Ex.P-1 is the copy of FIR, Ex.P.2 is the Complaint, Ex.P.3 is the Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.4 is the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, Ex.P.5 is the Wound Certificate, Ex.P.6 is the Charge Sheet, Ex.P.7 is the Notice under Section 133 of MV Act,
Ex.P.8 is the Reply to Notice, Ex.P.9 is the Medical Bills, Ex.P.10 is the X-ray Film and Ex.P.11 is the Adhar Card.

14. In the cross-examination of PW-1 by the counsel for Respondents No.1 and 2, he has similarly deposed that, at the time of accident he was riding the unoffending Honda Activa vehicle along with his son and sister's son as pillion riders.
His son was aged about 7 years and his sister's son was aged about 14 years.
He is possessing valid driving licence to ride the unoffending vehicle and insurance policy of that vehicle is in force.
Further he has denied that due to triple riding he lost his control over the vehicle and due to his fault caused the alleged accident.
Further he has denied that he has sustained simple injuries in the alleged accident.

Further he has deposed that after the alleged accident he was shifted to Dayananda Sagar hospital for first aid treatment and 11 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.7169/2024 thereafter he was shifted to KIMS Hospital for further treatment.
In the said KIMS Hospital the doctor has informed him that the medical expenditure will be more than Rs.70,000/-, as such he being a poor to pay such amount he went before local nati treatment.
Further he has denied that due to such treatment he was affected with infection.
Further he has denied that the alleged accident occurred due to his fault and no fault of the offending vehicle.
Further he has deposed that he is studied upto II PUC.
Further he has denied that his age is more than 40 at the time of the alleged accident.

Further he has deposed that prior to accident he was working as Office Assistant in Exteria Nutrition Company and he is getting salary of Rs.15,000/-
p.m. by way of cash.
Due to injuries sustained in the alleged accident he cannot able to do work.
Further he has denied that now also he is doing that job.
Further he has denied that he has not incurred Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenditure.
Further he has denied that he is hale and healthy and he is doing his regular work and activities as past without any pain or difficulties.
He has not undergone surgery.

Further he has denied that he was not possessing valid driving licence to ride the offending vehicle and the insurance policy of 12 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.7169/2024 that vehicle is not in force and in order to get more compensation in collusion with the police he has falsely implicated the rider of the offending vehicle and registered false case against him and he has produced concocted created documents and filed false evidence affidavit and deposing falsely.
During the cross examination Pw.1 has consistently deposed on the lines of the petition/prosecution case and he has made those versions, which could not be shattered in cross examination.

15. The Respondent No.2 contended that the accused is innocent and falsely implicated by the police, but in order to prove its version the Respondent No.2 has neither stepped into the witness box, nor produced documents and any how the Respondent No.2 cross- examined the PW-1.

Nawaz Khan vs Geethamma P on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33275874/
5 16.

On careful reading of Ex.P4/Motor Vehicle Accident Inspection Reports it specifies that the Motor Vehicle Inspector has been clearly opined that, the said accident did not occur because of the mechanical defects in respect of the said offending vehicle.

Further the said Inspector noticed the damages to the offending vehicle and opined that, front wheel assembly damaged, front fork assembly, handle are damaged and scratched, engine case, silencer, right 13 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.7169/2024 side body are scratched and front brake lever and rear view mirror are broken.
Further

the said Inspector noticed the damages to the unoffending vehicle and opined that, front mudguard, front body shield, head light wiser are broken and front fork assembly, handle, both sides body shield are damaged and scratched.

17. On going through the Ex.P-5/Wound Certificate it is seen that the Doctor opined that in the said alleged accident the Petitioner has sustained right commuted fracture of distal radius and the doctor opined that the injury is grievous in nature.

18. On going through the Ex.P-2/Complaint it is seen that on 15.08.2024 at about 11.00 a.m., near Somanahalli Toll, Kanakapura - Bengaluru main road, when the Petitioner was riding the unoffending Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-13-Y-4613 along with Muzamil Pasha and Sakib Khan as pillion riders, at that time the accused being the rider of the offending Bullet Motor Cycle bearing reg. KA-05-QD- 5332 instead of riding the same from Kanakapura - Bengaluru main road by approaching the left side toll, he drove the same in a opposite direction from Bengaluru - Kanakapura road toll in a high speed, rash and negligent manner so as to endangering 14 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.7169/2024 human life and dashed against the unoffending vehicle, as a result, Petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
Thereafter Petitioner was shifted to CDSIMER Hosptial, Harohalli and for higher treatment he was shifted to KIMS Hospital, Bengaluru wherein he was treated as inpatient.
The accident occurred due to negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.
19. On going through the Ex.P3/spot Mahazar it is seen that in pursuance of the alleged Ex.P2/complaint, on 17.08.2024, the informant has showed the place of incident to the police.
The police have conducted the detailed spot mahazar in the presence of panch witnesses and prepared spot sketch.
20. Admittedly, the accused is the rider of the offending vehicle and further admitted that,
Petitioner
sustained grievous injuries due to alleged accident caused by the offending vehicle in question.

The counsel for Respondent No.2 claimed that the said accused to be innocent and further the counsel for Respondent No.2 contended that, the alleged accident occurred due to fault of the rider/Petitioner of the unoffending vehicle and no fault of the accused/rider of the offending vehicle,
he was driving slowly and therefore he cannot be held to be 15 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.7169/2024 negligent.

On going through the prosecution papers, FIR, Spot mahazar, Wound Certificate and Charge Sheet and the evidence of PW-1 is specific to the effect that, the rider of the offending vehicle/accused is the reason for the said incident and at his instance, the incident took place and the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.

The evidence of Pw.1 is corroborated to the case of the prosecution and he has supported the manner of occurrence in his evidence in the court and the manner of occurrence is the same as alleged in the Ex.P2/complaint.

It seems that Pw.1 has clearly made those versions, which Nawaz Khan vs Geethamma P on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33275874/
6 could not be shattered in cross examination.

Therefore, considering the above discussed aspects collectively, it is the considered opinion of the Court that, the incident having been taken place in the manner asserted by the prosecution and the same being proved to have been taken place in the manner alleged by the prosecution, the accused drove the offending vehicle in a high speed, rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and at the spot dashed against the unoffending vehicle, as a result Petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

The evidence of Pw.1, Ex.P-1/FIR,
Ex.P-2/Complaint, 16 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.7169/2024 Ex.P3/spot mahazar, Ex.P.4/MVA Report,
Ex.P5/Wound Certificate and Ex.P-6/Charge Sheet clearly establishes that the alleged accident occurred at the spot.
It is not in dispute as to the aspect that, the Petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the alleged incident.
Because, for the above reasons collectively it is clear that, the accident happened due to rash and negligent act of the accused.
It is evident that injuries noted in the Ex.P5/Wound Certificate would be caused by a road accident.
At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
Matters being so, acts of the accused person clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 281 and 125(b) of BNS.

Thus because of such negligent act of the accused/rider of the offending vehicle, it resulted in the injuries of the innocent man/Petitioner aforesaid, as he/accused drove the said offending vehicle very rashly or negligently on the spot.
Therefore, the alleged accident occurred due to the fault of the accused/rider of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

Issue No.2 :- The Learned counsel for the Petitioner has contended that, the injured Petitioner was aged about 34 years and he was doing nutrition sales man and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m., and the Petitioner has incurred heavy expenses towards medical expenditure.

As such the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head of pain and suffering, mental agony, medical expenses,
special diet, conveyance, loss of future income due to disability, loss of amenities and loss of income during laid up period and prays to award the compensation as prayed in the petition.

22. On the other hand, the learned counsel for Respondent No.2 insurance company contended that even though the Petitioner claimed that his earning was about Rs.30,000/- p.m., the same is not established by the claimant by producing the documents.
Since the Petitioner has not established his income, he is not entitled for compensation towards such prospects and hence prays dismissal of the petition.

23. The petitioner contended that as on the date of the accident he was aged about 34 years and he relied on the Ex.P.11/Adhar Card of the Petitioner, wherein the date of birth of the Petitioner is shown 18 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.7169/2024 as 21.04.1982 and this accident was took place on 15.08.2024.
Hence it is clear that as on the date of the accident the Petitioner was aged about 42 years 3 months.
Hence the age of the Petitioner is considered as 42 years.
24. It is not in dispute that the Petitioner sustained injuries in the road traffic accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle by its rider/accused.
In the instance case the petitioner claimed that he was a nutrition sales man and earning sum of Rs.30,000/- p.m.

But he Nawaz Khan vs Geethamma P on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33275874/
7 has not produced single piece of document to prove his actual income.
In the absence of proof of income the notional income has to be assessed.

As per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, for the accident taken place in the year 2024, the notional income of the Petitioner is taken at Rs.15,750/-.
25.

In the chief examination of PW-4/Dr.Nagaraj.B.N., Orthopedic Surgeon deposed that in the alleged road traffic accident the petitioner has sustained right comminuted fracture distal radius,
first rib fracture and he was treated conservatively with below elbow slab and now the Petitioner complains of pain unable to lift weights and do his regular routine 19 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.7169/2024 work as before and on examination the Petitioner has wasting of right forearm muscle with restricted wrist joint movement.
Further deposed that recent X-ray of the right wrist shows united fracture and the Petitioner has sustained total disability of the right arm at 32% and whole body physical disability at 11%. PW-2
has produced Ex.P.12/Clinical Report and Ex.P.13/X-ray Film.
In the Cross examination of PW.2/doctor by the counsel for Respondent No.2 he has deposed that he has not a treated doctor of the Petitioner.
He was not having knowledge regarding what kind of followup treatment does the Petitioner has taken after his discharge and the fracture is united.
The Petitioner has not undergone surgery.
Further he has denied that due to the alleged accident the Petitioner has sustained simple injuries and he has not sustained any fracture.
Further he has denied that he has not examined the Petitioner properly and he has assessed the disability in his imaginary.
He do not know about the job of the Petitioner.
Further he denied that in order to help the petitioner he has assessed disability on the higher side and filed false evidence affidavit and deposing falsely.

As the occupation of the petitioner is considered as nutrition sales man, while doing his work the petitioner has to sit and stand for long time, he has to use his hands to lift the weights and to do his regular routine activities.
But due to injuries sustained in the alleged accident, he is not in a position to do work as earlier.
The doctor stated that the Petitioner has sustained total disability of the right arm at 32% and whole body physical disability at 11%.

Hence by considering the age, occupation,
nature of injury and the functional disability of the petitioner is considered as 11% to the whole body.
27. With regard to the quantum, age of the petitioner is considered as 42 years and the income is considered at Rs.15,750/- p.m.
As per Sarala Varma's Case the multiplier 14 is applicable and functional disability is considered at 11%.
On considering the avocation and age of the petitioner, the total loss of future income is calculated as (Rs. 15,750/- X 12 X 14 X 11/100) = Rs.2,91,060/-.

Hence,
an amount of Rs.2,91,060/- is awarded to the petitioner under the head loss of future income for the disability suffered by him in the accident.

28. In the alleged accident, as per Ex.P8 wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained right 21 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.7169/2024 comminuted fracture distal radius, first rib fracture and he was treated conservatively with below elbow slab, which shows that definitely the petitioner has suffered pain due to the injuries sustained in the accident, hence an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- is awarded Nawaz Khan vs Geethamma P on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33275874/
8
towards pain and suffering, mental agony.
29. Further due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has taken treatment at CDSIMER Hospital and KIMS Hospital, Bengaluru for treatment and also he has taken Nati Vydya treatment.
Therefore this court deems it appropriate to award Rs.25,000/- under head of special diet and conveyance.
30. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has suffered uncomfortable in his day to day life, hence an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- is awarded towards loss of amenities.
31. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the Petitioner would require atleast six months period to recuperate and to get back to his normal day to day activities.
Therefore the Petitioner would be entitled to Rs.94,500/- (Rs.15,750/- x 6 months) under the head loss of income during laid up period.
Further the Petitioner has produced hospital and medical bills, towards medical expenses as per Ex.P.9 for an amount of Rs.4,186/-.

Hence the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,186/-
under the head of hospital and medical expenses.

33. The details of compensation I propose to award are as under:
Sl. Compensation under different heads Amount in (Rs) No. 1 Loss of future income due to disability 2,91,060-00 2 Pain and suffering, mental agony 1,00,000-00 3
Special diet and conveyance 25,000-00 4 Loss of amenities 1,00,000-00 5 Loss of income during laid up period 94,500-00 6
Actual medical expenses 4,186-00 Total 6,14,746-00

The Petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.6,14,746/-.
34.
Hence the respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the award amount.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fixed on the respondent No.2/Insurance Company and it is directed to deposit the 23 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.7169/2024 compensation amount.
Thus I conclude that, the Insurance company/Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount along with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of filing of the claim petition.
Hence, I answer issue No.2 is partly in the affirmative.
35. Issue No.3:

In the result I proceed to pass the following: -
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the Petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.6,14,746/- (Rupees Six Lakhs Fourteen Thousand Seven Hundred and Forty Six only) with interest @ 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.

9 Further, Respondent No.2/ Insurance Company being insurer of the offending vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount together with 6% interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
After deposit, entire compensation amount with interest shall be released in favour of the 24 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.7169/2024 Petitioner under E-payment with proper verification and identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at  Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
Thereafter Petitioner was shifted to CDSIMER Hosptial, Harohalli and for higher treatment he was shifted to KIMS Hospital, Bengaluru wherein he was treated as inpatient.
It is contended that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.1 by admitting that she is the owner of the offending vehicle and denied the petition averments and her version is that, the offending vehicle was insured with Respondent No.2/Insurance company and any liability, i.e., fastened on her would have to be indemnify by the Respondent No.2 and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
The Respondent No.2 admitted the alleged accident and its version is that, the alleged accident occurred due to the negligence 9 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.7169/2024 and fault of the rider of the unoffending vehicle and no fault of the rider of the offending vehicle, however, slowly he may be driving and therefore he cannot be held to be negligent.
The burden to prove the framed issues lies on the Petitioner.
The counsel for Respondent No.2 claimed that the said accused to be innocent and further the counsel for Respondent No.2 contended that, the alleged accident occurred due to fault of the rider/Petitioner of the unoffending vehicle and no fault of the accused/rider of the offending vehicle,
he was driving slowly and therefore he cannot be held to be 15 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.7169/2024 negligent.
Hence the age of the Petitioner is considered as 42 years.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
On going through the prosecution papers, FIR, Spot mahazar, Wound Certificate and Charge Sheet and the evidence of PW-1 is specific to the effect that, the rider of the offending vehicle/accused is the reason for the said incident and at his instance, the incident took place and the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
The evidence of Pw.1 is corroborated to the case of the prosecution and he has supported the manner of occurrence in his evidence in the court and the manner of occurrence is the same as alleged in the Ex.P2/complaint.
Therefore, considering the above discussed aspects collectively, it is the considered opinion of the Court that, the incident having been taken place in the manner asserted by the prosecution and the same being proved to have been taken place in the manner alleged by the prosecution, the accused drove the offending vehicle in a high speed, rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and at the spot dashed against the unoffending vehicle, as a result Petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
It is not in dispute as to the aspect that, the Petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the alleged incident.
Because, for the above reasons collectively it is clear that, the accident happened due to rash and negligent act of the accused.
It is evident that injuries noted in the Ex.P5/Wound Certificate would be caused by a road accident.
At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
Matters being so, acts of the accused person clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 281 and 125(b) of BNS.
Thus because of such negligent act of the accused/rider of the offending vehicle, it resulted in the injuries of the innocent man/Petitioner aforesaid, as he/accused drove the said offending vehicle very rashly or negligently on the spot.
Therefore, the alleged accident occurred due to the fault of the accused/rider of the offending vehicle.
